name: Solanum
common_group: Nightshades (including horsenettles, buffalobur and cultivated tomato)

project_scope.study_context: Central Texas Hays County source-pool visual identification
project_scope.admission: Existing species preserved; S. nigrescens added 2026-10-20 by explicit owner approval as provisional comparative field learner, county range remains on hold. Added S. emulans on 2026-10-20 as PROVISIONAL user-directed field look-alike learner; no county-native claim. User-approved provisional S. interius field-ID learner 2026-10-20; Hays county proof not yet adjudicated. User-directed provisional S. nigrum European nonnative comparison 2026-10-20; no native count.
project_scope.science_gate: Retain PROVISIONAL county labels for unverified county-native species; bittersweet COMPARISON_NONNATIVE and tomato COMPARISON_CULTIGEN excluded from native counts.
project_scope.media_gate: Species photo records reflect current canonical cards, including conditional CC BY-NC noncommercial photos and one unverified-rights UT triquetrum archival image that must NOT be shown in public genus gallery. Genus gallery photo subset is separately curated; do not use historical seven-species photo count.

look_here_first: FIRST SPLIT: PRICKLY or UNARMED? PRICKLY: silver narrow foliage = silverleaf; broad green lobed leaves = western horsenettle; yellow flowers with ONE long curved anther and spiny fruiting calyx = buffalobur. UNARMED SCRAMBLER with red berries: compare Texas nightshade (triangular leaves, usually white flowers, separate anthers) against bittersweet (usually purple swept-back petals, tight anther cone); white bittersweet exists. UNARMED HERB with little white flowers/black berries: compare ANTHER length, ripe berry CALYX direction, pedicels and flower-cluster branching among five close species. Tomato is an obvious cultivated divided-leaf comparison. One color alone never establishes the species.

genus_diagnostics.flower: A five-parted usually star/rotate COROLLA (petals united at base) and five stamens, often with long yellow anthers clustered around central style. Colors and flower sizes vary widely, and some wild species have unequal anthers.
genus_diagnostics.anthers: Solanum often has PORICIDAL anthers: pollen escapes through little terminal pores; in some unarmed species those pores expand into longitudinal slits. Inspect anther shape, length and whether one is much longer: buffalobur has conspicuous unequal anthers (heteranthery). Ordinary front-flower photos do not resolve a pore.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Mostly alternate, simple to lobed or divided; several spiny horsenettles have star-shaped (STELLATE) surface hairs. Silverleaf nightshade has dense silvery scale-like hairs and narrow leaves; tomato has deeply divided foliage; scrambling S. triquetrum often has triangular/hastate leaves.
genus_diagnostics.stems: Some plants are UNARMED, some are prickly. Prickles are sharp epidermal emergences, NOT true branch thorns. Inspect stems, leaf veins, leaf underside and calyx; prickle number varies with age and individual.
genus_diagnostics.calyx: CALYX = outer SEPALS immediately below the corolla. In some Solanum it stays as a collar around an exposed berry; in S. americanum ripe calyx lobes bend far backward; in S. rostratum the fruiting calyx becomes enlarged and densely spiny enclosing the dry berry.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Solanum fruits are generally berries with multiple seeds: shiny black, shiny red, yellow-orange or variable domesticated tomato berries. Buffalobur encloses its dry berry with a prickly calyx, whereas silverleaf nightshade shows green-striped juvenile berries and later yellow-orange fruit. Never classify unknown berries as edible by fruit color.
genus_diagnostics.pollination: Most Solanum anther morphology is associated with vibration/buzz release of pollen by bees; do not infer pollinator identity from the flower image or treat it as a native host-count assertion.

shared_traits: Solanaceae family: flowers typically have fused 5-part corolla, stamens attached to the corolla, persistent calyx and a multi-seeded berry or capsule.
Solanum genus: starry flower morphology and clustered anthers commonly opening through terminal pores or short slits, berry-type fruit, highly variable leaves and prickles.
Species key: examine fruiting CALYX and anther equality with leaf hair/shape and armature — never use corolla color alone.
priority: 1 · First check armature and LEAVES: broad green, narrowly silver, deeply cut and prickly, or unarmed with triangular or ovate blades.

2 · Compare flowers: yellow BUFFALOBUR has ONE long curved anther; violet prickly species differ by foliage; red-fruited scramblers differ by REFLEXED purple corolla and close-packed anthers versus separate yellow anthers.
3 · For black-berried herbs, photograph open flowers with scale, short versus long yellow anthers, whole cluster and mature berry from the side showing green CALYX and pedicels.

4 · For red berries compare SCRAMBLERS: Texas nightshade has often 3–6 white flowers and arrowhead leaves; bittersweet has often 7–40 branching flowers with purple reflexed petals, but white forms exist.
5 · Use at least TWO structures. Unmeasured flowers, immature green fruit, a single red or black berry, or county occurrence rumors do not settle species.
6 · No taste tests, food advice or unrequested county-native certification. Hold unresolved morelloid IDs at genus/complex level.
warnings: Fruit color alone does not identify nightshades or prove edibility.
Black-nightshade anther sizes and green fruiting calyces overlap; flower + mature fruit + pedicel clues together are important.
Historical UT Solanum triquetrum voucher rights unverified: exclude its image from public genus gallery.
Joey Santore CC BY-NC 4.0 photos are usable only in the strictly noncommercial educational website with source/photographer credit.
Existing species native-range and introduced/cultivated statuses are preserved. The Hays county audit remains paused.

quick_key.if: Very prickly, deeply lobed foliage, YELLOW flower with FOUR short and ONE long curved anther
quick_key.then: Solanum rostratum · buffalobur — confirm prickly enlarged fruiting calyx

quick_key.if: NARROW silvery leaves, violet flower, possible prickles, green-striped young berry
quick_key.then: Solanum elaeagnifolium · silverleaf nightshade — check dense pale leaf surface

quick_key.if: Broad green sometimes lobed foliage, prickles, lavender flower, later yellow berry
quick_key.then: Solanum dimidiatum · western horsenettle — look at broad leaves and actual fruit

quick_key.if: UNARMED angled scrambler, TRIANGULAR/hastate leaves, few WHITE flowers with separate yellow anthers
quick_key.then: Solanum triquetrum · Texas nightshade — ripe red fruit photo still needed

quick_key.if: UNARMED scrambler, usually PURPLE REFLEXED petals, close yellow anther cone, RED berries
quick_key.then: Solanum dulcamara · bittersweet — rare WHITE flowers, so compare cluster and anthers

quick_key.if: Tiny WHITE flowers, SHORT anthers, shiny black berry whose little green calyx lobes bend BACK
quick_key.then: Solanum americanum · American black nightshade — inspect ripe calyx

quick_key.if: Tiny WHITE flowers, SHORT anthers, calyx APPRESSED/spreading over developing berry; fruit stalk may fall WITH ripe berry
quick_key.then: Solanum emulans · eastern black nightshade — mature berry photo still missing

quick_key.if: White flowers, relatively LONGER anthers, dark ripe berries with calyx CLOSE against fruit
quick_key.then: Solanum nigrescens · divine nightshade — use flower and ripe-fruit details together

quick_key.if: UNEVEN branching white-flower cluster, medium anthers, relatively LONG rounded green calyx lobes, larger black berry
quick_key.then: Solanum interius · plains black nightshade — Great Plains comparison, Hays occurrence unresolved

quick_key.if: White small flowers, comparatively THICKER fruit stalks, dark or greenish ripe berries; North American fruit typically lacks stone cells
quick_key.then: Solanum nigrum · European black nightshade — introduced, stone cells need actual dissection

quick_key.if: Cultivated aromatic-hairy plant with DIVIDED foliage, yellow flower and familiar varied domestic berries
quick_key.then: Solanum lycopersicum · tomato — comparison cultigen, not a native plant

comparison_cards.title: Prickly: Silverleaf vs Western horsenettle vs Buffalobur
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Start with leaf texture, shape and anther equality. Silverleaf: NARROW SILVER foliage. Western: BROADER GREEN often lobed foliage. Buffalobur: yellow flower with ONE markedly longer curved anther and spiny enlarged fruiting calyx.

field_matrix.elaeagnifolium: narrow, silvery from hairs; prickles variable
field_matrix.dimidiatum: broader green lobed leaves, usually prickly

field_matrix.rostratum: yellow, FOUR short and ONE long curved anther
berry enclosed in densely spiny enlarged calyx

field_matrix.dimidiatum: 2 real sources plus annotated look-alike panels; Vince Hale CC0 fruit

comparison_cards.caution: Prickle density varies. Do not claim single-anther pores or individual stellate hairs are visible in whole-plant photographs.

comparison_cards.title: Scrambling red berries: Texas nightshade vs Bittersweet
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Texas: sharply TRIANGULAR/HASTATE leaves, narrow angled stems, usually WHITE flowers with FREE yellow anthers in small clusters. Bittersweet: usually PURPLE strongly REFLEXED petals, CONNIVENT yellow anther cone, larger branching flower clusters. Both can have RED berries; occasional WHITE bittersweet makes flower color alone unreliable.

field_matrix.triquetrum: sharply triangular/hastate leaves; angled unarmed stems
field_matrix.dulcamara: ovate/heart-shaped, variable basal lobes; scrambling woody-based vine

field_matrix.triquetrum: usually white, distinctly separated anthers, often 3–6 flowers
field_matrix.dulcamara: usually purple swept-back (rare white), crowded anther cone, often 7–40 branched flowers

field_matrix.triquetrum: red fruit described; separate exact ripe-fruit photo missing
field_matrix.dulcamara: RIPE red berries, green-purple calyces and pedicels photographed

comparison_cards.title: SHORT anthers: American black vs Eastern black nightshade
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both unarmed, with small WHITE flowers and SHORT yellow anthers. Compare mature green fruiting CALYX: American has little lobes sharply REFLEXED backward, eastern has lobes APPRESSED/spreading on the berry. Eastern ripe fruit commonly detaches WITH its stalk; American leaves the stalk behind.

field_matrix.americanum: short plump anthers; comparatively shorter filaments
sharply BACK from ripe glossy black berry

field_matrix.americanum: often remains on cluster after mature berry falls

comparison_cards.caution: Do not use immature fruit alone to assign S. emulans; flower and fully mature fruit features are needed for high-confidence field IDs.

comparison_cards.title: LONGER anthers: Divine vs Plains vs European black nightshade
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Flowers overlap. Look for the UNEVEN flowering cluster and long rounded-tipped green calyx of plains black nightshade, more regular flowering and ripe calyx of divine, or thicker stalks and fruit stone-cell features of introduced European black nightshade. Combine several independent traits.

visual_comparison.title: Solanum: seven nightshades — first inspect anthers, leaves and fruit coverings
visual_comparison.subtitle: Nine installed and visually checked genus example photos from five species, plus two explicitly EXTERNAL Commons references of American black nightshade. S. dimidiatum CC BY-NC and S. triquetrum UT restricted sources are omitted from this public-reuse genus gallery. No anther-pore macro or arrow is certified.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: STAR FLOWER + ANTHERS → LEAF HAIRS/PRICKLES → CALYX/FRUIT. SILVER narrow leaves, one LONG curved anther, BLACK berry with reflexed sepals or RED-berried triangular-leaf climber?

part_examples.title: 1 · SEE a real nightshade flower
part_examples.look_for: A violet star-shaped COROLLA surrounds five yellow anthers gathered near the central STYLE. 'Corolla' means all the joined petals; 'anther' is pollen-making part of a stamen. The terminal pores are too small to verify in this image.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The close floral architecture is a better genus clue than whether the flower is purple, white or yellow.

part_examples.title: 2 · SPOT unequal anthers on buffalobur
part_examples.look_for: Find ONE extra-long curved lower anther below the four shorter yellow anthers. This is HETERANTHERY (two anther forms in one flower), which helps distinguish buffalobur among the local prickly Solanum.
part_examples.why_it_matters: One of the best real installed species-level identification macros in this group.

part_examples.title: 3 · NAME the prickly calyx
part_examples.look_for: The CALYX is the green outer whorl of sepals. As buffalobur fruits mature the calyx enlarges (ACCRESCENT) and becomes a vicious prickly BUR around the actual berry. Distinguish sepal and fruit rather than calling the whole prickly structure a seed pod.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates a spiny covering from the enclosed fruit; more informative than yellow flower color.

part_examples.title: 4 · COMPARE silverleaf's surface and habit
part_examples.look_for: Whole plant with light silver narrow leaves. The silver comes from dense fine star-shaped (STELLATE), often scale-like hairs; the individual hair rays need a 1 mm microscope photo. Do not claim this distant photo resolves rays.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates silverleaf from greener, broad-leaved horsenettles even before flowers appear.

part_examples.title: 5 · FOLLOW flower to young striped berry
part_examples.look_for: Real round pale-green fruits with DARK GREEN STRIPES and persistent green sepals, surrounded by silvery foliage. These fruits are immature and are not evidence that ripe fruit stays striped.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Connects the ovary to a fleshy berry and distinguishes it from the prickly-bur fruit enclosure.

part_examples.title: 6 · Compare the scrambling purple-flowered vine
part_examples.look_for: Purple petals sweep backward around a bright yellow cluster of stamens; some leaves have small basal lobes. This is the introduced bittersweet comparison. Compare white-flowered Texas nightshade's sharply triangular leaves using an independently cleared image later.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Prevents conflating two scrambling red-berried Solanum species merely because both have greenish eye spots.

part_examples.title: 7 · Compare the small unarmed herb
part_examples.look_for: A spreading green herb with alternate ovate leaves and no prickles. Ripe black berries and the short anthers are too small or absent in THIS photo; open source-linked fruit and flower references in the genus comparison instead.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Distinguishes a black-berried unarmed species from rough prickly nightshades, while highlighting what's still missing.

part_examples.title: 8 · NEED PHOTO — Western horsenettle green prickles
part_examples.role: Solanum dimidiatum broad green leaves, stem prickles and mature fruit
part_examples.look_for: Rights-cleared exact S. dimidiatum whole plant showing cream-yellow stem prickles, comparatively broad green and lobed leaves, flower, and a mature yellow berry. The existing single CC BY-NC flower view is retained in private species gallery but not reused in this public lesson until commercial-use restrictions are resolved.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The common lavender flower is NOT enough to distinguish it from silverleaf. Need side-by-side same-angle leaf/stem views.

part_examples.title: 9 · NEED PHOTO — Texas nightshade versus bittersweet
part_examples.role: Solanum triquetrum leaf, flower eye, red berry
part_examples.look_for: A clear rights-cleared exact S. triquetrum same-plant sequence: triangular to hastate leaves, white sometimes purple-tinged corolla with greenish central eye, and shiny red berries. The currently installed UT herbarium voucher is private-study source with reuse permission not confirmed.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Makes the extremely realistic scrambling red-fruited look-alike pair identifiable with real photographic tie-breakers.

visual_comparison.annotation_policy: Photo subjects are real and metadata supported. Structure names are look-for cues only unless the actual visible image shows the feature. No manual arrow target positions validated; rights-gated source photos remain excluded.
